Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
In what year did Stephen Hawking die?
Stephen Hawking: Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians.
In what year was Theobroma cacao discovered?
Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Mikoyan MiG-31: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-31 is the fastest known operational combat aircraft, with a top speed around 3,000 km/h (1,600 knots).
Which company manufactures CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: Chengdu Aircraft Industry Group. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
Who is credited with discovering Triangulum Australe?
Triangulum Australe: Américo Vespucio. Triangulum Australe is a small constellation in the far Southern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Ichthyosaurus?
Ichthyosaurus: Mary Anning. It is among the best known ichthyosaur genera, as it is the type genus of the order Ichthyosauria.
Who is credited with discovering Theobroma cacao?
Theobroma cacao: Christopher Columbus. Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Who is credited with discovering Krypton?
Krypton: William Ramsay. Krypton (from Ancient Greek: κρυπτός, romanized: kryptos 'the hidden one') is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

First coined as a term in 1852, this pattern of continued drinking despite its harms affected an estimated 283 million people worldwide as of 2016, according to the World Health Organization — name the condition?
Alcoholism is the continued drinking of alcohol despite the problems it causes.
This order of ray-finned fish is named for a modified fin ray that dangles like bait to lure in prey, much like a human with a fishing rod — what are they called?

Anglerfish are ray-finned fish in the order Lophiiformes. The majority are bottom-dwellers, being demersal fish, while the aberrant deep-sea anglerfish are pelagic, (mostly) living high in the water column.

This English science fiction writer, futurist, and undersea explorer received the 1961 Kalinga Prize, a UNESCO award for popularizing science, across a career spanning novels, essays, and television hosting — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke (16 December 1917 - 19 March 2008) was an English science fiction writer, science writer, futurist, inventor, undersea explorer, and television series host.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary one-sided facial paralysis of unknown cause can droop an eyebrow, alter taste, and make sounds painfully loud — what is it?
Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.
Element 107, a synthetic transactinide whose most stable known isotope lasts barely 2.4 minutes, takes its name from a famous Danish physicist — what is it?
Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Unlike ordinary weight loss from undereating, this illness-linked syndrome strips away muscle mass in ways good nutrition can't fully undo — what condition is it?
Cachexia is a syndrome that occurs in people with certain illnesses, causing muscle loss that cannot be fully reversed with improved nutrition.

Derived from the amino acid tyrosine and fifty percent bound to plasma proteins in your bloodstream, what class of neurotransmitter has a benzene ring topped with two hydroxyl groups plus a side-chain amine?

Catecholamine (abbreviated CA), most typically a 3,4-dihydroxyphenethylamine, is a monoamine neurotransmitter, an organic compound that has a catechol (benzene with two hydroxyl side groups next to each other) and a side-chain amine.
Grown for blue-flowered roadside roots that become a coffee substitute, or for bitter salad leaves like escarole and radicchio, which plant genus covers both chicory and endive?
Cichorium is a genus of plants in the tribe Cichorieae within the family Asteraceae.
This common bowel condition causes hard, dry stools passed fewer than three times a week, sometimes leading to hemorrhoids or fissures — what is it?
Constipation is a bowel dysfunction that makes bowel movements infrequent or hard to pass.
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded a company later acquired by MSC Software in 1998, then went on to co-found and lead a massively popular online gaming and creation platform — who is he?
David Baszucki (buh-; born January 20, 1963) is a Canadian-born American entrepreneur, engineer, and software developer.
First proposed as a model organism in 1901, this tiny insect species has become biology's workhorse for genetics research, and it's the one buzzing around your rotting fruit bowl. Name the species?
Drosophila melanogaster is a species of fly (an insect of the order Diptera) in the family Drosophilidae.
Practitioners of this zoological discipline have identified more than 1.3 million species within a single group of arthropods — what is it called?
Entomology (ntomon), meaning "insect", and (lgos), meaning "study", is the branch of zoology that focuses on insects.

This synthetic opioid is 50 to 100 times more potent than morphine and is now notorious in emergency medicine. Initially developed as a pain medication for cancer patients and post-surgical recovery, it works by activating opioid receptors — what is this drug?
Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'milky,' this term names any gravity-bound system of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter, ranging from tiny dwarfs to supergiants with a hundred trillion stars. What is it?
Galaxy is a system of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, dust, and dark matter bound together by gravity.
This large, semi-bitter citrus fruit originated in Barbados as an accidental 18th-century hybrid of the sweet orange and the pomelo, and has also been called the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit (Citrus paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.

Known as 'The Last Universalist' for mastering nearly every branch of his field, this French mathematician and physicist founded modern chaos theory through his study of the three-body problem — who is he?
Henri Poincaré (29 April 1854 - 17 July 1912) was a French mathematician, theoretical physicist, engineer, and philosopher of science.
A body-temperature emergency defined as a reading above 104°F, this condition kills roughly half a million people annually and is most commonly triggered by heat stroke — what is it called?
Hyperthermia is a condition in which an individual's body temperature is elevated beyond normal due to failed thermoregulation.

From deep-sea gribbles to the woodlice under your garden stones, members of this crustacean order share seven pairs of jointed limbs and brood their young in a pouch called a marsupium — what is the order?
Isopoda is an order of crustaceans. The order is divided into eleven suborders.

After leaving the company where he led industrial design for decades, this British-American designer founded the creative collective LoveFrom, which now works with Ferrari, Airbnb, and OpenAI. Who is he?
Jony Ive (born 27 February 1967) is a British-American designer.
This genus of deciduous conifers, unusual for shedding its needles each year, dominates the boreal forests of Siberia and Canada, making it the most abundant tree genus on Earth — what is it called?
Larch are deciduous conifers in the genus Larix, of the family Pinaceae.
Only about 35 atoms of this synthetic element (symbol Lv, number 116) had ever been made as of 2020 — named for a California national laboratory. Which element is it?
Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Sometimes nicknamed 'sea cows,' these large, fully aquatic herbivorous marine mammals can grow up to 13 feet long and include Amazonian, West Indian, and West African species — what are they called?
Manatee (family Trichechidae, genus Trichechus) are large, fully aquatic, mostly herbivorous marine mammals sometimes known as sea cows.
Its three main jobs are converting food into usable energy, building macromolecules like proteins and lipids, and excreting waste — the chemistry that keeps every living thing alive. What is it?
Metabolism (from) refers to the set of life-sustaining chemical reactions that occur within living organisms.
Named for the river near which its type fossil was found by a Dutch chalk quarry in the 18th century, this genus of marine reptile lived until the end of the Cretaceous — what is it?
Mosasaurus ("lizard of the Meuse River") is the type genus (defining example) of the Mosasauridae, an extinct group of aquatic squamate reptiles.
Named for a pioneering physicist's work on classical mechanics, this SI unit of force equals the push needed to accelerate one kilogram at one metre per second squared — name the unit?
Newton (unit) (symbol: N) is the unit of force in the International System of Units (SI).

These pouched mammals originated in South America and crossed into the north during the Great American Interchange; one species is so common in the U.S. that people just call it a 'possum.' What is it?
Opossum are members of the marsupial order Didelphimorphia endemic to the Americas.
This New York Times columnist of 24 years was the sole winner of the 2008 Nobel in economics for explaining the patterns of international trade and where economic activity clusters. Who is he?
Paul Krugman (born February 28, 1953) is an American economist who is the Distinguished Professor of Economics at the Graduate Center of the City University of New York.
Odorless when pure but reeking of rotting fish in technical grade, this colorless PH3 gas can burst into a luminous flame on contact with air — what highly toxic compound is it?
Phosphine (IUPAC name: phosphane) is a colorless, flammable, highly toxic compound with the chemical formula PH3, classed as a pnictogen hydride.
Though it looks like a small dolphin, this cetacean is actually more closely related to narwhals and belugas, and can be told apart by its flattened, spade-shaped teeth — what animal is it?
Porpoise are small dolphin-like cetaceans classified under the family Phocoenidae.
Its blossoms are a beloved symbol of early spring throughout East Asia, and its crunchy fruit is marketed globally as the Asian or nashi pear - which tree species?
Pyrus pyrifolia is a species of pear tree native to southern China and northern Indochina that has been introduced to Korea, Japan and other parts of the world.

A brilliant English anatomist who coined the word 'Dinosauria,' meaning roughly 'terrible reptile,' he accepted that evolution happened but was an outspoken critic of Darwin's account of it. Who was he?
Richard Owen (20 July 1804 - 18 December 1892) was an English biologist, comparative anatomist and palaeontologist.
Marked by hearing voices, disorganized thinking, and flat affect, this condition is diagnosed by observed behavior rather than any objective test — what is it?
Schizophrenia is a mental disorder characterized variously by hallucinations (typically, hearing voices), delusions, disorganized thinking or behavior, and flat or inappropriate affect.
Long, thin and transparent, this hydrozoan drifts through the ocean as a colony of specialized zooids that together handle feeding, floating and jet propulsion — what marine organism is this?
Siphonophore (from Ancient Greek (siphn), meaning "tube" and - (-phros), meaning "bearing") are cnidarian animals of the hydrozoan order Siphonophorae.

Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes' and 'kernel,' this genus of spherical, Gram-positive bacteria grows in grape-like clusters and can survive with or without oxygen — what's the genus called?
Staphylococcus (staphul), meaning "bunch of grapes", and (kkkos), meaning "kernel" or "Kermes", is a genus of Gram-positive bacteria in the family Staphylococcaceae from the order Bacillales.
Though some scientists place it in its own genus, Acrocodia, the Malayan species is usually still classified within this genus of tapir — name this genus?
Tapirus is a genus of tapir which contains the living tapir species.
This intensely itchy, contagious fungal skin infection produces a red, scaly rash with a curved border across the groin and buttocks, mostly in men — what is it?

Tinea cruris (TC), also known as jock itch, is a common type of contagious, superficial fungal infection of the groin and buttocks region, which occurs predominantly but not exclusively in men and in hot-humid climates.
This bodily fluid, produced by the kidneys to flush out urea and other waste, can also serve a second life as a nitrogen-rich fertilizer for soil — what is it?
Urine is the fluid excreted by the kidneys of vertebrates to clear the bloodstream of excess water and metabolic by-products including urea, uric acid, and creatinine.
Native to Eastern and Southern Africa, this large antelope genus includes two species — one black, one blue — whose lineages diverged roughly a million years ago — what animal is it?
Wildebeest (VIL-), also called gnu (NOO or, NEW), are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa.

This symptom can stem from something as mild as gastroenteritis or as serious as a ruptured aortic aneurysm or ectopic pregnancy, yet its exact cause goes unexplained in about a third of cases — what symptom is this?
Native to China and Taiwan, this fast-growing deciduous tree can reach 15 meters in 25 years and has become notorious in North America as a host plant for the invasive spotted lanternfly. What is it?
Ailanthus altissima: Deciduous tree in the quassia family.
This military pilot became his country's first astronaut when he flew to the International Space Station aboard a 2024 mission — who is he?
Alper Gezeravcı: Turkish fighter pilot and astronaut (born 1979)
Commonly called windflowers, which genus of the buttercup family is native to every continent except Australia, New Zealand, and Antarctica?
Anemone: Genus of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Also nicknamed the cross spider or diadem spider for the white markings on its back, this orb-weaver is native to Europe but was introduced to North America — what species is it?

Araneus diadematus: Species of spider. The spider species Araneus diadematus is commonly called the European garden spider, cross orbweaver, diadem spider, orangie, cross spider, and crowned orb weaver.
The third-largest fish in its family, behind Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this species is unusual for surviving spawning and returning to sea to breed again — which fish?
Atlantic salmon: Species of fish. The Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.
Named for the physicist who shared a 1903 Nobel Prize with Pierre and Marie Curie, this SI unit measures one radioactive decay event per second — which unit?
Becquerel: SI derived unit of radioactivity.
Despite its name, only the soles of this tawny, spotted feline's paws are actually dark — and at just 35 to 52 centimetres long, it ranks as Africa's smallest wild feline species — what animal is it?
Black-footed cat: Small wild cat native to Southern Africa.
Also known as warble flies or gadflies, the larvae of which insect family live as internal parasites in mammal flesh or gut, with one species routinely infesting humans?
Botfly: Parasitic insect. Dermatobia hominis is the only species of botfly known to parasitize humans routinely, though other species of flies cause myiasis in humans.
He piloted the Lunar Module Eagle in 1969 to become the second person to walk on the Moon, and after Jim Lovell's death in 2025 became the oldest living astronaut — who is he?
Tetravalent and able to form four covalent bonds, this element known since antiquity ranks as the fourth most abundant in the universe by mass — which one is it?
Carbon: Chemical element with atomic number 6 (C)

Greek for "head-feet," fishers nickname these inkfish for their ink-squirting trick; their arms are muscular hydrostats modified from the primitive molluscan foot. Which marine class includes the octopus, squid, and nautilus?
Cephalopod: Class of mollusks. The study of cephalopods is a branch of malacology known as teuthology.
Made in the skin after sun exposure and also known as vitamin D3, this compound is converted by the liver and kidneys into forms that help the body absorb calcium. What is it?

Cholecalciferol: Vitamin D3, a chemical compound. Cholecalciferol, also known as vitamin D3, colecalciferol or calciol, is a skin-made vitamin D that is found in certain foods and used as a dietary supplement.
This scale insect that feeds on prickly pear cacti produces carminic acid, the basis of the red dye carmine used in lipstick and food coloring — what is it?
Cochineal: Species of insect producing the crimson dye carmine.
Known historically as blue vitriol, this bright blue crystalline compound with the formula CuSO4 forms an octahedral complex when dissolved in water — what compound?
Copper(II) sulfate: Chemical compound. It forms hydrates CuSO4·nH2O, where n can range from 1 to 7.
Named for the ancient Greek word for a ship's helmsman, this transdisciplinary field studies feedback loops and circular causal processes across engineering, biology, and social systems — what is it?

Cybernetics: Study of circular causal processes. Cybernetics' transdisciplinary character means that it intersects with a number of other fields, resulting in a wide influence and diverse interpretations.
This autoimmune disease attacks both the skin and skeletal muscles, causing a rash alongside worsening weakness, and is often linked to distinct myositis-specific autoantibodies — which condition?
Dermatomyositis: Autoimmune disease of skin and muscle. Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.

Originally developed to compete for a USAF aerial-tanker contract it lost to Boeing's Stratotanker, this four-engined jetliner instead entered airline service with Delta in 1959 — what aircraft was it?
Douglas DC-8: American four-engined jet airliner family.
This membrane-bound series of protein complexes shuttles electrons through redox reactions, building a proton gradient that ultimately powers the synthesis of ATP — what's it called?
Electron transport chain: Energy-producing metabolic pathway.
Named from the Greek for 'red skin,' this bacterial infection produces a raised, sharply defined, bright-red rash typically on the face or legs — what's the condition?
Erysipelas: Human disease from a bacterial infection of the skin.
Also nicknamed the 'baum' or 'sweet' variety, this mustelid species ranges across much of the continent into Asia Minor, the Caucasus, and parts of Iran, Iraq, and Syria. What animal is it?
European pine marten: Species of mammal in the mustelid family.

This branch of Islamic scholarship interprets the Quran and sunnah through jurist reasoning, producing fatwas — while sharia itself is seen as unchanging, this human field is considered fallible. What is it called?
Fiqh: Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, whereas sharia is considered immutable and infallible by Muslims, fiqh is considered fallible and changeable.
This cold-weather injury turns skin white or waxy-blue after tissue actually freezes, often preceded by a tingling, numb warning stage called frostnip — what is it?
Frostbite: Effect of low temperature on skin and other tissues.

Predicted by Mendeleev in 1869 under the placeholder name 'ekasilicon' and discovered in 1886 by Clemens Winkler, this metalloid element was named for its discoverer's home country — what element is it?
Germanium: Chemical element with atomic number 32 (Ge)
One of China's 'Four Great Domestic Fish,' this herbivorous freshwater species was later introduced to Europe and the US to control aquatic weeds — which fish?
Grass carp: Species of fish. This Asian carp is the only species of the genus Ctenopharyngodon.
The son of a famous physicist and his first wife, this Swiss-American engineer taught hydraulic engineering at Berkeley and became renowned for research on sediment transport — who is he?

Hans Albert Einstein: Swiss-American engineer and educator. Hans Albert Einstein (May 14, 1904 – July 26, 1973) was a Swiss-American engineer, the second child and first son of physicists Albert Einstein and Mileva Marić.
In this condition, part of the stomach slips upward through the diaphragm into the chest, often triggering acid reflux, heartburn, or trouble swallowing — what is it?
Hiatal hernia: Entrance of abdominal organs into the middle chest through the diaphragm.
Also called prussic acid, this toxic, flammable liquid with the formula HCN boils just above room temperature and serves as an industrial precursor to plastics and mining chemicals — what is it?
Traditionally drawn from the leaves of Indigofera plants and now mostly made synthetically, this blue compound is the color most associated with denim and blue jeans — what is it?
Indigo dye: Chemical compound, food additive and dye.
Before he proposed that the Earth behaves like one self-regulating living system, this English independent scientist built the detector that first revealed CFCs lurking in our atmosphere. Who was he?

An Alberta-born clinical psychologist and University of Toronto professor, he drew huge attention in the late 2010s for his cultural and political views — self-identifying as a classical liberal. Who is he?
Also called German turnip despite not being related to true turnips, this stout cabbage cultivar can be eaten raw or cooked, stem and leaves alike — what vegetable?
Kohlrabi: Biennial cultivar of wild cabbage.
Also known as Peruvian ginseng, this Andean root crop is grown at high altitude in Peru and Bolivia and exported worldwide as a dietary powder — what plant is it?
Lepidium meyenii: Plant species native to South America.
Developed under Kelly Johnson's Skunk Works team after the discovery of Germany's Me 262, this aircraft became the first jet fighter flown operationally by U.S. forces in World War II — which jet?
Lockheed P-80 Shooting Star: First jet aircraft in U.S. operational service.
Best known in its heptahydrate form as Epsom salt, this white crystalline compound (MgSO4) is also used in agriculture to fix soils deficient in an essential plant nutrient — what compound is it?
Magnesium sulfate: Chemical compound with formula MgSO4.
Born in Erfurt in 1864, this German jurist-turned-scholar became one of the founding figures of sociology before a breakdown following his father's death halted his teaching — who was he?
Max Weber: German sociologist, jurist, and political economist (1864–1920)
Originally known as amethopterin, this chemotherapy drug also treats autoimmune conditions like rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, and can end ectopic pregnancies — what is it?
Sold under the brand name Provigil, this first-line narcolepsy treatment boosts dopamine without the euphoria or addiction risk of classic stimulants like amphetamine — what is it?
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this genus of bacteria is naturally resistant to beta-lactam antibiotics that target cell-wall synthesis — which genus?
Mycoplasma: Genus of bacteria. Mycoplasma is a genus of bacteria that, like the other members of the class Mollicutes, lack a cell wall (peptidoglycan) around their cell membrane.

Published in the Principia Mathematica, this principle holds that every particle in the cosmos attracts every other with a pull proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the squared distance between them — which principle is it?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Classical statement of gravity as force.
First described by Linnaeus in 1758, this medium-sized spotted wild cat hunts armadillos and opossums at twilight across a range from the southwestern US to South America — what cat is it?
Ocelot: Species of wild cat. It is native to the southwestern United States, Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean islands of Trinidad and Margarita.

Most members of this order of over 200 species are solitary night hunters with broad heads, binocular vision, and feathers tuned for silent flight — though oddballs like the burrowing kind break the mold. What are they?
Owl: Birds from the order Strigiformes.
Nicknamed the empress tree for its fast growth and showy foxglove-like blooms, which East Asian hardwood has become an invasive species across the Eastern US?
Paulownia tomentosa: Species of deciduous tree classified in its own family.

Combining textual criticism, literary criticism, history, and linguistics, this scholarly field traces its classical roots to the libraries of Pergamum and Alexandria in the 4th century BC — what is it?
Philology: Study of language in historical sources.
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Sold under the brand name Phenergan, this first-generation antihistamine treats allergies and nausea but has also seen recreational misuse alongside codeine — which drug?
Promethazine: Sedating antihistamine. Promethazine is taken by mouth (oral), as a rectal suppository, or by injection into a muscle (IM).
Once one of America's leading rocket experts with an MIT aeronautics degree, he was deported to China in 1955 and went on to father that nation's space program — which aerospace engineer?

Nicknamed the 'Jug,' this WWII American fighter-bomber carried eight .50-caliber machine guns and weighed up to eight tons fully loaded, making it one of the heaviest fighters of the war — which aircraft?

Republic P-47 Thunderbolt: Family of fighter aircraft. The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt (nicknamed the "Jug") is a World War II-era fighter aircraft produced by the American company Republic Aviation from 1941 through 1945.
Also known as sixth disease, this childhood viral infection typically strikes before age three with a sudden fever followed by a pink rash lasting under three days — what's the condition called?
Roseola: Human disease caused by human herpesviruses.

Sometimes nicknamed the "seven-year itch," this contagious infestation by a tiny burrowing mite spreads fastest in crowded places and announces itself with fierce itching and a pimple-like rash — what is it?
Nicknamed the 'Human Computer' for her lightning mental arithmetic, this Indian writer also authored one of the earliest studies of homosexuality in India, back in 1977 — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi: Indian writer and mental calculator (1929–2013)

Historically mined in vast deposits and nicknamed 'Chile saltpeter,' this white, water-soluble alkali metal compound is used in fertilizers, fireworks, meat preservation, and solid rocket fuel. What is it?
Sodium nitrate: Chemical compound. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.
Derived from the Greek word for 'narrow,' this medical term describes the abnormal tightening of a blood vessel or other tubular structure — what is it?
Stenosis: Medical condition. Stenosis (from Ancient Greek στενός (stenós) 'narrow') is the abnormal narrowing of a blood vessel or other tubular organ or structure such as foramina and canals.
Defined by a single skull opening behind each eye socket that anchors larger jaw muscles, this major branch of the amniote family tree includes all mammals and their extinct kin — which clade?
Synapsida: Clade of tetrapods. Synapsida is a diverse group of tetrapod vertebrates that includes all mammals and their extinct relatives.
Also sold under the name dronabinol, this principal psychoactive compound in cannabis is prescribed to relieve chemotherapy-induced nausea and HIV/AIDS-related appetite loss — what is it?
Tetrahydrocannabinol: Psychoactive component of cannabis. It is the principal psychoactive constituent of Cannabis and one of at least 113 total cannabinoids identified on the plant.
Sitting between cells and organs in the body's organization, this assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix takes its English name from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology): Group of similar cells performing a specific function.
Roughly three times stiffer than steel and nearly as hard as diamond, this gray powder is sintered into cutting tools, armor-piercing bullets, and jewelry — what compound is it?
Tungsten carbide: Hard, dense and stiff chemical compound.
Unlike arteries, most of these thin-walled blood vessels carry deoxygenated blood back toward the heart — what are they?
Vein: Blood vessels that carry blood towards the heart.
A slow-moving filter-feeder and the largest known fish alive — the biggest reliably recorded stretched nearly 19 metres — this is the only living member of its family. What is it?
Whale shark: Largest living species of fish. The whale shark (Rhincodon typus) is a slow-moving, filter-feeding carpet shark and the largest known extant fish species.

Distinguished by a fatty hump on its shoulders and a large dewlap, this heat-tolerant type of domestic cattle originated in South Asia and holds religious significance in parts of the world — what is it?
Zebu: South Asian domestic cattle. The zebu (Bos indicus), also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia.

The symbol for barium is Ba. Barium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ba and atomic number 56.
